topic.title: Matching and Allocation with Learned Structure
topic.overview: Matching algorithms pair participants or resources while respecting feasibility, preferences, and timing. This topic includes online and stochastic matching, stable matching, graph correspondence, and learning-augmented algorithms. Data can guide dual variables, predictions, or aggregation strategies, but the resulting allocation still needs a meaningful quality guarantee.
topic.whyItMatters: Decisions often arrive before future requests are known, and a locally attractive match can consume a resource needed later. Structural information can improve practical allocation without assuming an omniscient view of the entire sequence.
topic.evolution: Early representatives investigate discrete relaxation for graph matching. Later work develops distributed allocation, learned advice, and sharper stochastic guarantees. Recent studies address ties, calibration, and dynamic coarsening; a heart-transplant simulation illustrates how grouping resources can yield strong performance under an explicit model rather than merely simplifying the problem heuristically.
openQuestions: Which learned predictions improve matching when their errors are systematic?
How can allocation guarantees account for fairness and strategic responses as well as efficiency?
